coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 6–8 miles, Z2 only (140 bpm ceiling). Your resting HR jumped 15 bpm and recovery score is 53/100—both flags that your nervous system hasn't fully settled from last week's 31.1-mile block. Wednesday normally calls for vert work, but not today. You're 30 days out; sharpness matters less than arrival fresh. Keep it flat, conversational, dial back the perceived effort. This run is about blood flow and clearing metabolic debt, not stimulus.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You logged 9 hours of sleep at 78% efficiency—decent volume but fragmented. Pair that elevated resting HR with a deliberate carb surplus today: 6–8g/kg of body weight (assume ~150–170g for you). Emphasis on easy-to-absorb carbs (rice, pasta, oats, fruit) at lunch and dinner. Your glycogen is likely still partially depleted from the 12-miler last week; replenish now while you're in taper, not on race eve.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep quality is the priority this week. That 78% efficiency suggests fragmentation—check your sleep environment (cool, dark, no blue light 1 hour before bed). Aim for 8.5–9.5 hours tonight with consistency. Your elevated resting HR (81 vs. 66-day avg) suggests incomplete parasympathetic recovery; prioritize 10–15 minutes of low-intensity breathing work or restorative stretching post-run. No sauna, no ice baths—just passive recovery and nutrition.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the taper gauntlet—the point where fitness plateaus and doubt creeps in. You've built the engine over 29 weeks. Today's cutback isn't loss; it's preparation. The Julian Alps 50K demands mental toughness on altitude and sparse aid; that toughness comes from arriving rested, not from squeezing one more workout. Trust the plan. Your 12-miler at 132 bpm showed good aerobic efficiency—that work is banked.
